Hi Alex / Samantha,

Thanks again for the time today — really appreciated the walkthrough of FinEdge's fraud-detection pipeline and the constraints around latency and data residency. Quick recap and next steps below so we're all aligned.

Recap
- Goal: Reduce inference latency on customer-facing fraud checks while keeping unit cost under control.
- Key constraints: EU data residency for transaction logs; peak traffic in US/APAC; occasional large batches for end-of-day scoring.
- Success metric: 95th percentile latency < 120ms for normal traffic profile; cost target TBD in MAP.

Proposed next step: technical deep dive + demo with our SE (Aditya) to cover: model variants, quantization tradeoffs, routing/fallback config, and deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

Scheduling — rotating slots idea (short version)
I know coordinating across US/EU/APAC is painful. To keep momentum, two options:
1) Pick a single slot that works for all (hard).
2) Rotate meeting times weekly so the burden is shared across your regional teams.

Candidate 45-min slots (all times shown in local zone + UTC):
- Option A (US-friendly): Tue 11/9 11:00 AM PT / 2:00 PM ET / 19:00 UTC (works for US and late EU)
- Option B (EU-friendly): Wed 11/10 9:30 AM CET / 8:30 AM UTC / 2:30 AM PT (early for US)
- Option C (APAC-friendly): Thu 11/11 9:00 AM SGT / 1:00 AM UTC / Wed 11/10 5:00 PM PT

If you like the rotating approach, we typically suggest a 3-week rotation: week 1 = US-friendly, week 2 = EU-friendly, week 3 = APAC-friendly. That way each region occasionally gets a friendly time.

Attachments: demo-agenda.pdf (high-level demo + deep-dive topics), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (draft MAP).

Can you let me know which option you prefer (single slot vs rotating), and any of the candidate times above that work for your team? If helpful, here's a Calendly link to pick a time directly: https://calendly.com/redwood/camila-demo-30min

Thanks!

Camila Reyes
